children.translated_text: <s>Sevyasevakopadeśa</s> (Instruction on Masters and Servants).
Composed by the great poet, the illustrious <s>Kṣemendra</s>.
To the great ornament that removes the darkness of craving,
homage to the jewel of contentment, the destroyer of the poison of servitude!
Having abandoned their own affairs, with eyes brimming with tears, let the noble ones
compose this instruction on the service of masters and servants.

children.text: darpād ekaḥ paro lobhād dvāv andhau sevyasevakau |
children.translated_text: One blinded by arrogance, the other by greed — both master and servant are blind;
disfigured by the heat of wealth and the distortion of wretchedness, who sees whose face?

children.text: durvāramohalobhāndho yadi na syād ayaṃ janaḥ |
children.translated_text: If these people were not blinded by irresistible delusion and greed,
who would endure the faces of the wealthy, contorted with cruel anger?

children.text: yaḥ pṛthvīm api darpāndho na paśyati puraḥsthitām |
children.translated_text: He who, blinded by arrogance, does not see the earth itself standing before him —

children.text: sa dainyalaghutāṃ yātaṃ kathaṃ sevakam īkṣate ||
children.translated_text: how would he look upon a servant reduced to the lightness of wretchedness?

children.text: agatiṃ vāhayaty eko badhiraṃ stauti cāparaḥ |
children.translated_text: One makes a cripple walk, the other praises a deaf man —
alas, in this world the shameless master and servant are objects of ridicule!
The petitioner, always dismissed from afar with a mere grunt,
fallen from virtue, devoid of action — the servant feels no agitation.

children.text: manye sukṛtinā tena bhāgīrathyāṃ kṛtaṃ tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: I consider that man of good merit who performed austerities at the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges),

children.text: vairāgyabhāgī rathyāṃ yaḥ sevāsu na vigāhate ||
children.translated_text: who, endowed with detachment, does not plunge into servitude on the street.
By the narrated accumulation of hardships, as if by a ripening curse,

children.text: sevātāpena pacyante na hy aduṣkṛtino narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people are cooked by the heat of servitude — for those without misdeeds are not [so afflicted].
The fame of those whose minds are free from the sin of wretchedness shines forth —
those who have not made their heads vessels for the stain of the mud of servitude.
Gazing at his belly, mute with wretchedness, while bowing to the master,

children.text: praveṣṭuṃ sevakaḥ śaṅke vilakṣaḥ kṣitim īkṣate ||
children.translated_text: the servant, I suspect, looks at the ground in embarrassment, [wishing] to enter it.

children.text: sevādhvajo 'ñjalir mūrdhni hṛdi dainyaṃ mukhe stutiḥ |
children.translated_text: The folded hands upon the head are the banner of servitude; in the heart is wretchedness; on the lips, praise —
for those seized by the demon of desire, how great is this mockery!
By the eye of the lord, disturbed with anger at an untimely arrival,
the servant quickly attains a burnt state, as if [struck] by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love).
He has offered libations of water for the death of further insults of servitude —
he who, having entered the army, has made his body a vessel for the sword.
The wretched servant-<s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird), tormented by living on scraps,
forever devoted to the hope of clouds, cranes his neck and withers away.
Devoid of contentment, the bee abandons the blossoming forest;
the servant, out of greed for gifts, serves even an elephant (i.e., a dangerous master).
Tormented by service to a dull master, observing the severe vow of hypocrisy like a crane,
the servant attains with difficulty a momentary pleasure.
Though always desiring advancement, he faces downward from the breaking of his pride —

children.text: yat satyam ubhayabhraṣṭas triśaṅkur iva sevakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in truth, fallen from both, the servant is like <s>Triśaṅku</s> (suspended between heaven and earth).
Engaged in the sale of his own flesh, whipped by the master's cane,
the spiritless servant perishes during night duties.
Sleeping on the ground, without food, wounded by cold, wind, and heat,
the servant, though observing the vow of a sage, experiences the torments of hell.

children.text: karoti sevakaḥ sevāṃ tāvad āśām ivāyatām |
children.translated_text: The servant performs service as long and extended as desire itself,
until he is parted from youth, which knows the taste of enjoyment.

children.text: cakṣur dvāry añjalau pāṇiḥ stutau jihvā natau śiraḥ |
children.translated_text: The eye at the door, the hand in folded salutation, the tongue in praise, the head in bowing —
alas, the servant's body has been made an instrument for others!
Alas! The servant, reduced to lightness by the humiliation of begging,

children.text: sevāpaṅkapade magno yad anviṣṭo na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: sunk in the muddy path of servitude, seeks but does not find [what he desires].
For the creature who finds no rest and no dispassion, who dries up with long sighs,
servitude is unbearable like old age, causing contraction.
It snaps like a wet string; it wilts in an instant like a garland;
servitude does not bear fruit — it perishes with the cutting of days.
For those whose limbs are wasted by servitude, who wither on the royal streets,
afflicted by the poison of intense craving — their refuge is the water of tranquility.

children.text: lobhasya mohādhvani vṛddhabhāve jātā durāśāśayitasya sevā |
children.translated_text: Servitude arises in the old age of greed, on the path of delusion, born from one asleep in false hope;

children.text: adhomukhī sā satataṃ salajjā jaratkumārīva na kasya śocyā ||
children.translated_text: she is forever downcast and ashamed, like an old maiden — who would not pity her?
Revolving in emptiness like desire, averse to contentment like craving,

children.text: divāniśaṃ karṣaṇadīrgharajjuḥ sevā surāṇām api dainyabhūmiḥ ||
children.translated_text: servitude is a long rope of toil day and night — a ground of wretchedness even for the gods.

children.text: nisargavandhyāsu phalāśayā ye kurvanti sevāsu sadā prayatnam |
children.translated_text: Those who always make effort in services that are barren by nature, hoping for fruit,

children.text: kṛṣipravṛttāḥ śaśaśṛṅgakoṭyā khananti mūrkhāḥ khalu svasthalīṃ te ||
children.translated_text: engaged in cultivation with the tip of a hare's horn — those fools indeed dig their own ground.

children.text: antaḥsthite 'py ātmani yaiḥ kriyante sevāpravṛttaiḥ puruṣaiḥ praṇāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those men engaged in servitude who make prostrations though the Self dwells within —

children.text: dugdhābdikallolini kūlakacche tṛṣṇāturās te jalam arthayante ||
children.translated_text: they, afflicted with thirst, beg for water on the muddy shore of the billowing ocean of milk.
When on the banks of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges), in the forest groves, there are great trees bowing with fruit,
capable of quenching hunger, heat, and thirst — what need is there for the humiliation of addiction to wretched servitude?

children.text: nityaprasaktyā na sṛjaty avajñāṃ na laulyagarhāgaṇanāṃ karoti |
children.translated_text: Through constant attachment, he does not create contempt, nor does he count the reproaches for greed;

children.text: atyantayācñāsu na yāti khedaṃ bhikṣābhujām pātram ato nu sevyam ||
children.translated_text: he does not become weary at excessive begging — therefore the begging-bowl of mendicants is indeed the [best] master to serve.

children.text: jayanti te svasti namo 'stu tebhyaḥ prabhūpraṇāmacyutamānaratnam |
children.translated_text: Victorious are they, may blessings be upon them, whose jewel of honor is not lost through bowing to lords,

children.text: sevāprayāsavyasaneṣu mithyā rathyārajobhāgi śiro na yeṣām ||
children.translated_text: whose heads do not falsely partake of the dust of the street in the addiction to the toil of service.

children.text: kiṃ rājabhir durjanajanmajālavyāptair avāptair api kaṣṭadṛṣṭaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What use are kings, entangled in the web of births of wicked people, even when obtained, painful to behold?

children.text: santy eva sevyā bhuvi bhūbhṛtas te taṭeṣu yeṣāṃ munayo niviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are indeed worthy masters on earth — those mountains on whose slopes sages have settled.
For those tormented by thirst, enveloped by dust (<s>rajas</s>), scorched by the fire of the chaff-heap of service,
beneficial for peace is the water of the heavenly river (<s>Tridaśāpagā</s>), purified by the friendship of the matted locks of the moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>).

children.text: utsṛjya tīvraṃ viṣayābhilāṣaṃ saṃtoṣapoṣaṃ kuśalo bhajasva |
children.translated_text: Abandoning intense desire for sense objects, skillfully cultivate the nourishment of contentment;

children.text: ity arthyamānaḥ sukhasevayāyam ātmāiva sarvaṃ sudhiyāṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: thus being entreated through the easy service [of contentment], the self itself gives everything to the wise.

children.text: ekasya jāne sukhabhogabhājaḥ ślāghyasya sevāvyasanaṃ nivṛttam |
children.translated_text: I know of one praiseworthy being who shares in blissful enjoyment and whose addiction to service has ceased,
because he is always devoid of phallus and belly, and free from begging that which should not be begged for — [namely] <s>Rāhu</s>.
Entered into the vow of service as if into a fast unto death, with his whole being certain of the destruction of life,

children.text: dvāḥsthaiḥ prayatnena nivārito 'pi na durgrahaṃ muñcati naṣṭasaṃjñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even though carefully prevented by the doorkeepers, he does not release his stubborn grip, having lost all awareness.

children.text: tamo'dhvatāpena ca cintayā ca śitena dainyena ca piṇḍitāṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: His body contracted by the heat of the dark path, by anxiety, and by the cold of wretchedness,
the foolish-minded one endures the vow of service, partaking of a thousand sorrows in hope of happiness.

children.text: gacchāmi gacchāmi dinaṃ gataṃ me dine gato 'haṃ na nṛpo 'dya dṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am going, I am going! The day has passed for me, the day is gone and I have not seen the king today!'

children.text: iti bruvāṇasya sadā janasya jīrṇātarāṃ tasya tanur na tṛṣṇā ||
children.translated_text: Thus speaks the person always; his body grows ever more decrepit, but not his craving.

children.text: vicchedakārī sahasā kathānām anīpsito dīpa iva praviṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Breaking conversations abruptly, entering unwanted like a [gust upon a] lamp,

children.text: saṃsaktavastrāntaramakṣikeva na sevakaḥ kasya karoti duḥkham ||
children.translated_text: like a fly that has gotten into the folds of one's garment — what servant does not cause suffering?
Fuming [with rage], hostile to the eyes, causing earache through the succession of flattery,

children.text: kusevakaḥ pādatale 'valagnaḥ pade pade kaṇṭakatām upaiti ||
children.translated_text: the bad servant, clinging to the sole of the foot, becomes a thorn at every step.

children.text: ekaḥ kham eva kṣitim īkṣate 'nyaḥ sa nirjanārthī sa ca gāḍhalagnaḥ |
children.translated_text: One looks only at the sky, the other at the earth; one desires solitude, the other clings tightly;

children.text: svasvārthitā tasya bhṛśaṃ sa cārthī kathaṃ sa sevyaḥ sa ca sevako 'stu ||
children.translated_text: each has his own selfish interests intensely, and each is a petitioner — how can one be the master and the other the servant?

children.text: chāyāgraho mūrta ivānuyāyī sthitaś ciraṃ vṛścikaniścalaś ca |
children.translated_text: Like an embodied shadow, following everywhere, standing motionless for long like a scorpion,
falling upon one at wrong times, like the lotus in the mechanism of a game-device — such is the importunate servant.

children.text: visṛjyamāno 'py aniśaṃ na yāti tīvroparodhapraṇayena mūrkhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though dismissed constantly, the fool does not go, with his intense love of obstruction;

children.text: bhartuḥ prasāde vihitaprayatno jātaḥ paraṃ pratyuta kopahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made efforts for the master's favor, he becomes instead only a cause of anger.
Through sighing, long-drawn breaths, and persistent [signs], announcing the effort of his agitated comings and goings,
because of excessive intrusion, this stubborn seeker, being rejected, comes to futility.
adorned with the glory of jewels, moons, horses, and elephants,
In this great ocean named the profound royal court,
poison (<s>kālakūṭa</s>) to attain sovereignty from the king.
the foolish-minded one, driven by hope, swallows much
O deaf one, this is a row of thorny <s>khadira</s> trees — it is fruitless, move on!'
'Stop, stop! O traveler, this is not a row of bending mango trees!
the servant, bound by the noose of great expectation, does not abandon his bad service.
Though told this in many ways through indirect suggestions,

children.text: pramlānā sarasatvam eti na punar māleva lagnātapā
bhagnā kācamayīva saṃdhighaṭanā yogena na śliṣyati |
children.translated_text: once broken, like something made of glass, it cannot be mended through joining.
Once wilted, like a garland exposed to heat, it does not regain freshness;
devoid of oil [affection], perishes through the gusts of sighing born of weariness.
Service, like a flame in a poor man's house, barely sustained,

children.text: kas tvaṃ gatvara sevakas tvaritatā kasmāt prabhur dṛśyate
lābhaḥ kas tava tatra vetrivipulāghātaiḥ śirastāḍanam |
children.translated_text: 'What is your gain there?' 'Getting my head struck with great blows of canes.'
'Who are you, rushing one?' 'A servant.' 'Why the hurry?' 'The lord is to be seen.'

children.text: kiṃ mṛdgāsi mudā viśālacaraṇair mithyaiva rathyām imām

children.translated_text: 'Friend, we are being mocked by the illusion of the grand mansion of a barren king.'
'Why do you tread this street with broad feet so joyfully?'

children.text: suptākarṣaṇadāma dhāma mahato mohasya dainyasya vā

children.translated_text: that rope for pulling the sleeping, abode of great delusion or wretchedness —
He who endures the affliction of service day and night in hope of a mere scrap of wealth —

children.text: saṃkṣubdhaṃ makarākaraṃ praviśati śrīratnalabdhyai na kim ||
children.translated_text: arising from the depths containing the blazing submarine fire (<s>Vaḍavāgni</s>), for the sake of obtaining gems of wealth?
does he not [effectively] enter the turbulent ocean full of crocodiles, agitated with garlands of waves
intent on watching the door, yet being pushed away by the attendants,
Through the entanglements of futile, excessive comings and goings, untiringly rushing with intensity,
the servant, who betrays all misfortunes, will attain the likeness of a dog.
resorting only to the stratagem of forcing entry at the front — [becoming] a repository of affliction and humiliation,
of the cruelly creaking door-bolts, who guard the entrance,
Struck severely by the doorkeepers with firm arms, enraged by the squeezing
inquires within of those observing a vow of silence, who have come out without any opportunity [to speak].
the servant, hunching over, eager for quick entry through the gaps between people's knees,

children.text: dvāre ruddham upekṣate katham api prāptaṃ puro nekṣate

children.translated_text: he seizes upon verbal pretexts; when [the servant] has departed, he enumerates faults over the slightest offense — a <s>Yama</s> (god of death) [in person];
He blocks [the servant] at the door; when [the servant] somehow arrives before him, he does not look; during a petition, he closes his eyes like an elephant;

children.text: sa svāmī yadi sevyate marutaṭe kiṃ naḥ piśācaiḥ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: what have demons done to us on a windswept desert?
if such a master is served,

children.text: bhaktiṃ bhūtisamudbhave na tu bhave dhyānaṃ dhane nātmani |
children.translated_text: his devotion is not in Being but in the arising of prosperity; his meditation is not on the Self but on wealth;
Always in the royal court, he does not worship the venerable, but worships the doorkeepers;

children.text: śrīhetor bata niṣphalaṃ prakurute sarvaṃ jaḍaḥ sevakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: alas, the dull servant does everything fruitlessly for the sake of fortune!
his reflection on the seen and unseen is directed at the king, not at his own proper action —

children.text: sā tīvraṃ jaḍanimnapātanaratā no nityasaktā tvarā
rathyāpaṅkakalaṅkitaṃ na vadanaṃ na dvārapālaiḥ kaliḥ |
children.translated_text: that is no face stained by the mud of the street; that is no quarrel with the doorkeepers —
That haste, which delights in dragging the dull one down steeply, is not constant devotion;

children.text: yasmiṃs taccirasevakaḥ pravitataṃ puṇyaṃ vanaṃ gamyatāṃ
krūrās te na bhavanti tatra vikṛtakrodhoddhatāḥ pārthivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There those kings, distorted and agitated with cruel anger, do not exist.
in whatever [place] where one has long been a servant, let one go to the holy forest!

children.text: haṃho kaṣṭavinaṣṭa sevaka sakhe khinno 'si poṣāśayā
rāgaś ced vibhave tad eṣa kupatiḥ klībaḥ kim āsevyate |
children.translated_text: If there is attachment to wealth, why is this wicked, impotent lord served?
Ho there, friend servant, lost in misery, you are wearied by the hope of sustenance!

children.text: sevyaḥ ko 'pi maheśvaraḥ sa bhagavān yasya prasādekṣaṇair

children.translated_text: by whose unimpaired gracious glances, <s>Marutta</s>, lord of the winds, was made an object of compassion!
There is someone worthy of service — that blessed great lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>),

children.text: rājñām ajñatayā kṛtaṃ yad aniśaṃ dainyaṃ tad utsṛjyatāṃ

children.translated_text: Let the dust accumulated by bowing at [their] feet be washed off in the water of contentment!
The wretchedness that is perpetually caused by the ignorance of kings — let that be abandoned!

children.text: yatsmṛtyā na bhavanti te sumanasāṃ bhūyo bhavagranthayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the remembrance of whom, those knots of worldly existence no longer bind the wise!
Let the supreme contentment, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Being), consisting of pure consciousness, be served —
cutting the bonds of the noose of desire, quenching intense craving with the pure waters of tranquility,
Abandoning lavish service of kings who enjoy solitary pleasures and share in deception,

children.text: sthitva śuddhe samādhau kim aparam amṛtaṃ mṛgyatāṃ jyotir antar

children.translated_text: upon seeing which, with the heavy burden of dense darkness destroyed, the glory of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is attained!
abiding in pure <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) — what other nectar is there? Let one seek the inner light,

children.text: vṛttyā jīvati lokaḥ sevāvṛttir nijaiva keṣāṃcit |
children.translated_text: The world lives by its livelihood; for some, service itself is their own livelihood.

children.text: asthāne tīvratarā nindyā tu tadarthināṃ sevā ||
children.translated_text: But servitude that is excessively intense and misplaced is blameworthy for those who seek it.
By the one named <s>Kṣemendra</s>, devoted to the gratification of the learned, filled with the essence of the service of contentment,

children.text: kṣemendranāmnā sudhiyāṃ sadaiva sukhāya sevāvasaraḥ kṛto 'yam ||
children.translated_text: this occasion of [teaching about] servitude has been composed always for the happiness of the wise.
Thus ends the <s>Sevyasevakopadeśa</s> (Instruction on Masters and Servants), composed by the great poet, the illustrious <s>Kṣemendra</s>, also known as <s>Vyāsadāsa</s>.
